subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw accept these breaking gateway-protocol and validator-export changes for beta and prospective package consumers before a public npm compatibility contract exists?
rationale: The branch deliberately removes and reshapes externally consumable protocol surface; code inspection alone cannot establish whether the asserted beta-only compatibility window is the intended release policy.

options.title: Approve the pre-publication break
options.body: Confirm that the affected protocol families and validator exports have no supported shipped consumers, then require focused client proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve a temporary compatibility layer
options.body: Keep deprecated wire aliases or validator exports through a documented transition window if any beta or package consumer is supported.

options.title: Split the publication preparation
options.body: Land metadata and dead-code cleanup separately while deferring wire-shape changes until the release contract is explicitly decided.

recommendation.title: Approve the pre-publication break
recommendation.body: Confirm that the affected protocol families and validator exports have no supported shipped consumers, then require focused client proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author is the only concrete routing candidate in the supplied protocol-area history, though maintainer confirmation remains required.
